- Direct repository inspection: tests/android/composeNavigationRoutes.spec.ts (205 lines, read for pattern), tests/index/androidNavigationIncremental.spec.ts (234 lines, listed), tests/android/androidNavigationProject.spec.ts (85 lines, listed), full `tests/` directory listing for android/compose-related file inventory, package.json scripts (test, typecheck, build, verify)

Existing tests (closest owners, confirmed present in the repository):
- tests/android/composeNavigationRoutes.spec.ts — closest unit-test-owner pattern: builds an in-memory temp fixture app (mkdtempSync + writeFileSync), runs buildIndex + detectAndroidProject, then calls the analyzer function directly and asserts on its return value. This exact pattern (not vi mocks, not CLI invocation) is the pattern for the new src/android/buildAndroidComposeSemanticProject.ts unit/component tests.
- tests/android/androidNavigationProject.spec.ts — closest orchestration-level unit-test owner (tests buildAndroidNavigationProject's artifact-assembly behavior, not just the Compose-route sub-scanner) — pattern for artifact-shape/detected-gating tests.
- tests/index/androidNavigationIncremental.spec.ts — closest incremental-regression test owner (--incremental add/change/remove-evidence scenarios against runIndexCommand). Pattern for the new incremental-regression tests (PSE-029).
- tests/integration/androidV110Artifacts.spec.ts, tests/integration/androidV110Incremental.spec.ts — closest full-pipeline integration-test owners (multiple Android artifacts asserted together via a single index run). Pattern for artifact-presence/absence + manifest-registration integration tests (PSE-026).
- tests/graph-diff/androidGraphDiffCompatibility.spec.ts — confirms the existing convention for asserting an Android artifact does NOT participate in graph-diff; NOT extended in Batch 1 (graph-diff integration is out of scope), but its existence is evidence that "compatibility" tests for new Android artifacts follow a known, low-effort pattern if ever needed later.
- No existing test file targets Compose *declaration* extraction (only Compose *route* extraction exists today) — a new focused test file is required per external contract Section 16 ("a new focused Compose analyzer test file only if no existing test owner is appropriate"), justified: declaration-level extraction is a materially different responsibility (annotations/scope/body-range/child-calls vs. route-string extraction) with no existing exact owner.

Test matrix / test responsibilities:

test responsibility ID: TST-001
description: extracts a simple public top-level @Composable declaration
  criticality: critical
  traces to: BEH-001, BEH-002, BEH-008, PSE-012, PSE-013, PSE-017
  setup: temp Android+Kotlin fixture app (writeAppScaffold pattern) with one Kotlin file containing `@Composable fun SimpleScreen() { Text("hi") }`
  action or trigger: call buildAndroidComposeSemanticProject() directly with the built symbolIndex/androidProject
  expected result: artifact.detected === true; declarations has exactly one entry with scope 'top-level', visibility 'public', isPreview false, name 'SimpleScreen'
  test level: unit
  behavior under test: BEH-001/BEH-008 (exact-annotation-gated extraction)

test responsibility ID: TST-002
description: extracts a top-level composable with parameters and records statically available parameter summaries
  criticality: noncritical
  traces to: PSE-004, PSE-017 (parseParameterList)
  setup: `@Composable fun Greeting(name: String, modifier: Modifier = Modifier)`
  action or trigger: run analyzer
  expected result: declaration.parameters has two entries with name/typeText populated for the statically simple case
  test level: unit
  behavior under test: derived value (ComposeParameterSummary)

test responsibility ID: TST-003
description: distinguishes a private top-level composable from a public one
  criticality: critical
  traces to: INV-002, BEH-008
  setup: `private @Composable fun InternalPiece()` alongside a public one in the same file
  action or trigger: run analyzer
  expected result: the private declaration's visibility === 'private', scope still 'top-level' (not 'function-local')
  test level: unit
  invariant under test: INV-002

test responsibility ID: TST-004
description: extracts a named function-local composable and sets its enclosingDeclarationId
  criticality: critical
  traces to: INV-002, BEH-008, PSE-013 (declarationStack)
  setup: a non-Composable enclosing `fun Screen() { @Composable fun InnerPiece() { ... }; InnerPiece() }`
  action or trigger: run analyzer
  expected result: two extraction outcomes depending on pseudocode's exact contract — assert only the function-local composable is extracted (scope: 'function-local', enclosingDeclarationId references the enclosing frame's tracked id even though the enclosing plain `fun Screen()` is itself not a declarations[] entry, since it's not Compose-annotated) and a childCall from... N/A here since child-call resolution requires the enclosing function itself be a tracked composable; this case exercises enclosingDeclarationId population against a non-Compose enclosing frame specifically, per pseudocode-packet PSE-013's explicit "enclosing frame's OWN id is only referenced, never itself added to declarations unless separately Compose-annotated"
  test level: unit
  invariant under test: INV-002, PSE-013 enclosing-frame tracking

test responsibility ID: TST-005
description: distinguishes a private top-level composable from a function-local composable (both are "not public top-level API" in casual terms, but structurally different)
  criticality: critical
  traces to: INV-002 (explicit non-conflation requirement)
  setup: one file containing both a `private fun` top-level composable and a same-named-pattern function-local composable in different enclosing functions
  action or trigger: run analyzer
  expected result: the two are never conflated: scope fields differ ('top-level' vs 'function-local'), and visibility/enclosingDeclarationId differ accordingly
  test level: unit
  invariant under test: INV-002

test responsibility ID: TST-006
description: identifies @Preview + @Composable declarations
  criticality: critical
  traces to: BEH-009
  setup: `@Preview\n@Composable\nfun ScreenPreview()`
  action or trigger: run analyzer
  expected result: isPreview === true; a same-file non-preview composable has isPreview === false
  test level: unit
  behavior under test: BEH-009

test responsibility ID: TST-007
description: extracts a direct, exactly-resolved parent-to-child composable call
  criticality: critical
  traces to: BEH-010, INV-003, PSE-016, PSE-018
  setup: `@Composable fun Parent() { Child() }` and `@Composable fun Child() {}` in the same file
  action or trigger: run analyzer
  expected result: Parent's declaration.childCalls has exactly one entry with calleeDeclarationId === Child's id
  test level: unit
  behavior/invariant under test: BEH-010, INV-003

test responsibility ID: TST-008
description: does not record a child-call for an unresolved/ambiguous callee
  criticality: critical
  traces to: INV-003, PSE-018 (0-match and >1-match branches)
  setup: (a) `Parent()` calls `SomeUnknownCall()` with no matching same-file declaration; (b) two function-local composables both named `Item` in different enclosing functions, both called from a third composable
  action or trigger: run analyzer
  expected result: (a) no childCalls entry and no warning (silent omission per BEH-010); (b) no childCalls entry recorded for the ambiguous name AND a warning string is present in artifact.warnings
  test level: unit
  invariant under test: INV-003

test responsibility ID: TST-009
description: does not infer a child-call from capitalization/naming similarity alone
  criticality: critical
  traces to: 14.6 (external contract), INV-003
  setup: `Parent()` calls `Row(...)` (a structural region, uppercase, but not itself a declared composable in this file)
  action or trigger: run analyzer
  expected result: Row is recorded only in structuralRegions, never in childCalls (since it does not exactly match a same-file Compose-declaration name)
  test level: unit
  boundary under test: structural-region vs. child-call disambiguation

test responsibility ID: TST-010
description: extracts each of the seven fixed structural UI-region calls without overclaiming route/runtime facts
  criticality: critical
  traces to: BEH-011
  setup: one composable body containing Scaffold, LazyColumn, LazyRow, Column, Row, Box, and NavHost calls (NavHost included specifically to prove no route is extracted from it in this artifact)
  action or trigger: run analyzer
  expected result: structuralRegions has exactly 7 entries, one per kind, in body order; no route/destination fields anywhere on the entry (type-level check plus a runtime assertion the object has no such keys)
  test level: unit
  behavior under test: BEH-011

test responsibility ID: TST-011
description: rejects a false-positive @Composable-looking annotation inside a line comment
  criticality: critical
  traces to: BEH-012, "Conservative parsing" (external contract 14.5), negative fixture requirement
  setup: `// @Composable fun Fake() {}` followed by real unrelated code
  action or trigger: run analyzer
  expected result: no declaration extracted for "Fake"; no false warning
  test level: unit
  failure mode under test: comment-text false positive

test responsibility ID: TST-012
description: rejects a false-positive @Composable-looking text inside a string literal
  criticality: critical
  traces to: BEH-012, external contract 14.5
  setup: `val s = "@Composable fun NotReal() {}"`
  action or trigger: run analyzer
  expected result: no declaration extracted for "NotReal"
  test level: unit
  failure mode under test: string-literal false positive

test responsibility ID: TST-013
description: does not classify an anonymous composable lambda or a higher-order-function-returned composable as a named declaration
  criticality: critical
  traces to: external contract Section 2.3 "must not claim support", BEH-012
  setup: `val lambda: @Composable () -> Unit = { Text("x") }` and `fun rememberScreen(): @Composable () -> Unit = { ... }`
  action or trigger: run analyzer
  expected result: no declaration entries produced for either pattern; declarations array unaffected by their presence in the file
  test level: unit
  boundary under test: named-function requirement (FUNCTION_PATTERN match required, not just annotation presence)

test responsibility ID: TST-014
description: does not extract an unsupported member composable inside a class/object body (records a warning if the pattern is annotation-recognizable)
  criticality: noncritical
  traces to: external contract Section 2.3/2.5, BEH-012
  setup: `class ScreenHost { @Composable fun Render() {} }`
  action or trigger: run analyzer
  expected result: no declaration entry for Render(); a stable warning string referencing the unsupported nesting context is present in artifact.warnings
  test level: unit
  failure mode under test: unsupported-nesting-context degrade-to-warning path (PSE-013 scope === null branch)

test responsibility ID: TST-015
description: captures complete deterministic source ranges across multiline annotations and multiline signatures
  criticality: critical
  traces to: BEH-007, BEH-013, "Source ranges" (external contract 14.4)
  setup: an annotation split across two lines is not realistic in Kotlin (annotations are single-token) — instead: a multiline function signature (`@Composable\nfun LongSignature(\n  a: String,\n  b: Int\n) {\n  ...\n}`)
  action or trigger: run analyzer
  expected result: sourceRange.startLine === the @Composable annotation's line; sourceRange.endLine === the closing brace's line; range fully contains the signature and body
  test level: unit
  behavior under test: BEH-013, PSE-014

test responsibility ID: TST-016
description: captures a complete source range for an expression-body declaration
  criticality: noncritical
  traces to: PSE-014 expression-body branch, "expression-body functions where safely supported" (external contract fixture requirement)
  setup: `@Composable fun Label(text: String) = Text(text)`
  action or trigger: run analyzer
  expected result: sourceRange spans exactly the single logical statement; declaration is still extracted with a valid, non-degenerate range
  test level: unit
  behavior under test: PSE-014 expression-body rule

test responsibility ID: TST-017
description: captures correct adjacent-declaration boundaries (no bleed between two back-to-back composables)
  criticality: critical
  traces to: BEH-013, "adjacent declarations" (external contract fixture requirement)
  setup: two `@Composable fun` declarations directly adjacent with no blank line between them
  action or trigger: run analyzer
  expected result: each declaration's sourceRange.endLine is strictly less than the next declaration's sourceRange.startLine (or annotation-inclusive start line); no overlap
  test level: unit
  invariant under test: "a declaration record whose sourceRange does not fully contain its own annotations+signature+body" (behavior-model.txt Invalid states)

test responsibility ID: TST-018
description: deterministic IDs and ordering across two runs of byte-identical input
  criticality: critical
  traces to: INV-005, PSE-020, PSE-028
  setup: run buildAndroidComposeSemanticProject() twice over the same fixture without any filesystem mutation between runs
  action or trigger: compare both results
  expected result: declarations arrays are deeply equal except createdAt/any explicitly-timestamped field; IDs identical; array order identical
  test level: unit
  invariant under test: INV-005

test responsibility ID: TST-019
description: deterministic tie-breaking for duplicate declaration keys within one file
  criticality: noncritical
  traces to: PSE-020 ordinal-suffix rule
  setup: a malformed/contrived fixture with two identically-named top-level composables in one file (not valid idiomatic Kotlin, but the scanner must not crash or produce colliding IDs)
  action or trigger: run analyzer
  expected result: first occurrence gets the unsuffixed id, second gets an ordinal-suffixed id; no ID collision; no crash
  test level: unit
  invariant under test: "two declaration records sharing the same id" (Invalid states)

test responsibility ID: TST-020
description: gates entirely on androidProject.detected (Compose scanning does not run for a non-Android Kotlin project)
  criticality: critical
  traces to: BEH-001 gate, behavior-model.txt "Unresolved design questions" resolution
  setup: a plain Kotlin project fixture (no AndroidManifest.xml/Gradle Android evidence) containing a valid `@Composable fun Screen()`
  action or trigger: detectAndroidProject() returns detected:false; run buildAndroidComposeSemanticProject() with that result
  expected result: artifact.detected === false, declarations === [], no analyzer work performed beyond the immediate early return
  test level: unit

test responsibility ID: TST-025
description: --incremental adds a supported Compose declaration -> artifact appears on next incremental run
  criticality: critical
  traces to: BEH-015, TRN-001, PSE-029
  setup: index a fixture app with no Compose declarations under --incremental, then add a Kotlin file with a supported composable and re-run --incremental
  action or trigger: two sequential `runIndexCommand({incremental:true})` calls (or CLI invocations) with a file added between them
  expected result: after run 1, android-compose-semantic.json absent; after run 2, present with the new declaration; cache mode reflects the existing changed-file classification (incremental-partial or incremental-change-detected-full-rebuild, whichever the existing eligibility logic selects — this test asserts artifact correctness, not which specific cache mode was chosen, since that choice is pre-existing, unmodified behavior)
  test level: integration
  behavior/transition under test: BEH-015, TRN-001

test responsibility ID: TST-026
description: --incremental changes a supported Compose declaration's body -> artifact content refreshes with a new/changed declaration entry
  criticality: critical
  traces to: BEH-015, PSE-029
  setup: index a fixture with one composable, then modify its body (add a child call) and re-run --incremental
  action or trigger: two sequential incremental runs with an edit between them
  expected result: the declaration's childCalls (or sourceRange) reflects the edit after run 2; no stale cached content
  test level: integration
  behavior under test: BEH-015

test responsibility ID: TST-027
description: --incremental removes the last supported Compose declaration -> artifact is removed on the next refresh-reaching run
  criticality: critical
  traces to: BEH-003, TRN-002, PSE-029
  setup: index a fixture with one composable, delete the file (or the declaration) and re-run --incremental
  action or trigger: two sequential incremental runs with a deletion between them
  expected result: android-compose-semantic.json is absent after run 2 (removed by refreshIndexOutput's blanket-cleanup-then-conditional-rewrite, since the second run's writeIndexArtifacts call omits androidComposeSemantic)
  test level: integration
  transition under test: TRN-002

test responsibility ID: TST-028

  criticality: noncritical
  traces to: TRN-003, INV-005

  action or trigger: two sequential incremental runs with only a non-Kotlin change between them
  expected result: android-compose-semantic.json content is unchanged (modulo createdAt) between run 1 and run 2
  test level: integration
  invariant under test: INV-005, no separate cache introduced

Test level assignment summary:
- unit: TST-001..TST-020 (src/android/buildAndroidComposeSemanticProject.ts direct function calls, new test file tests/android/composeSemanticDeclarations.spec.ts)
- integration: TST-021, TST-022, TST-025..TST-029 (full runIndexCommand() pipeline, new/extended tests under tests/index/ and tests/integration/)
- regression (existing, unmodified): TST-023, TST-024, TST-030, TST-031
- build/static-analysis: TST-032

Required verification commands (grounded in package.json, confirmed present):
- Focused: `npx vitest run tests/android/composeSemanticDeclarations.spec.ts` (new file, exact name TBD at implementation)
- Focused: `npx vitest run tests/android tests/index/androidComposeSemanticIncremental.spec.ts tests/integration` (new + closest existing Android suites)
- Full: `npm test` (vitest run, whole suite)
- Static: `npm run typecheck`, `npm run build`, `npm run verify`
- Explicitly NOT run: `npm run benchmark:retrieval` (retrieval behavior unchanged, external contract Section 16/20 exclusion)

Coverage gaps / risks not covered and why:
- Compose Multiplatform (non-Android) Compose usage is not covered — explicitly out of scope per the behavior-model.txt gate resolution (Compose scanning only runs when androidProject.detected); if this gate resolution is later found wrong, this entire test surface would need to expand, but that is a product-scope question, not a Batch 1 test gap.
- Cross-file child-call resolution is not covered by any positive test (only same-file, per pseudocode-packet's PSE-018 same-file-only assumption-guard) — TST-008(a) proves the negative (unresolved, not guessed) but there is no test proving cross-file calls are *correctly* left unresolved with a *specific* warning, since PSE-018 specifies silent omission (not a warning) for the plain 0-match case, which already includes cross-file calls; this is intentional and consistent with BEH-010, not a gap.
- Extremely large Kotlin files (near/at MAX_SCAN_LINES) are not covered by a dedicated performance/truncation test in this packet; the existing buildComposeNavigationRoutes.ts precedent's own truncation-warning behavior is trusted by analogy but not independently re-verified for the new analyzer. Flagged as a noncritical gap; may be added opportunistically during implementation if low-cost, not required for PASS.

Status: complete
